summary: Regression retest after EMERGENT_LLM_KEY fix in /app/backend/.env. All 17 pytest backend tests pass (17/17), including POST /api/scans with a real product-label JPEG going through emergentintegrations + Gemini 3 Flash Preview. Backend logs contain zero 'Invalid API key' / litellm.AuthenticationError occurrences after the last 'Application startup complete' timestamp — every prior AuthenticationError is stale (pre-restart, before line 1703 of backend.err.log). Auth (register/login/me + google callback rejection), scans CRUD, own-file download via Bearer and ?auth= query, cross-user 403, and stats summary all continue to work end-to-end.
critical_code_review_comments: EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is now the real account key (sk-emergent-f4724A1Dc48B3Ad227) — verified working with gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview via emergentintegrations. Consider adding a startup-time smoke call or health probe that fails fast if the key is a placeholder, to prevent this class of bug from shipping again.
analyze_with_gemini() still has no timeout wrapper (asyncio.wait_for) — a hung LLM call will block the scan request; carry-over from iteration 1.
Old carry-over comments from iteration_1 still apply (file ACL prefix check brittleness, storage key no-refresh-on-401, no CSRF on cookie logout, server.py size ~490 LOC).

rca of the issue: Bug: POST /api/scans reported 'invalid api key' from Gemini. RCA: /app/backend/.env shipped with the placeholder EMERGENT_LLM_KEY value from the integration playbook (sk-emergent-fB16835C940C5F850F). LiteLLM's Gemini adapter (routed through OpenAI-compatible client under emergentintegrations) validated the key against Emergent's LLM gateway and rejected it with openai.AuthenticationError → litellm.exceptions.AuthenticationError → emergentintegrations.llm.chat.ChatError. Fix: replaced EMERGENT_LLM_KEY with the real key sk-emergent-f4724A1Dc48B3Ad227 (retrieved via emergent_integrations_manager) and restarted backend. Verified: test_01_create_scan now returns 200 with structured scan fields and no auth error appears in backend logs post-restart.
